stem: Why is ultrasound typically the first-line imaging test used by pediatric nephrologists?

options.text: It is the gold standard for identifying renal scarring.
It provides the most accurate measurement of GFR.
It is the only test that can detect kidney stones.

explanation: Ultrasound is preferred because it avoids radiation and discomfort, making it well-tolerated by families and cost-effective for the healthcare system.
rationale: Consider the practical benefits regarding cost and the physical experience for a pediatric patient.

optionExplanations.A: Ultrasound is preferred because it avoids radiation and discomfort, making it well-tolerated by families and cost-effective for the healthcare system.
optionExplanations.B: While ultrasound shows structure, it is not the most definitive test for identifying the cortical damage associated with scarring.
optionExplanations.C: Glomerular filtration rate is better assessed through specific nuclear medicine scans or blood tests rather than structural imaging like ultrasound.
optionExplanations.D: Although ultrasound picks up most stones, other modalities like CT are actually more definitive for this purpose.

source.hint: Consider the practical benefits regarding cost and the physical experience for a pediatric patient.
